findings.claim: Grading loop 0040A6E0 selects the first non-0x8000 plane-1 height in an X-major then Y-minor search of its padded rectangular bounds, or falls back to the plane-0 object anchor height with 0 promoted to 1.
findings.limitations: Integer rotation boundary rounding and exact authored workspace fixtures are not dynamically verified.

findings.claim: The object grader always writes the selected height to the bounded region, while class 0x50/0x51 selects surface 6 and class 0x52/0x53 selects surface 7 independently; classes 2/3 do not issue the material write.
findings.limitations: Overlapping material writes can also be affected by other editing operations outside this grader.

findings.claim: The grader processes 80 zone list heads in ascending numeric order, following each head-linked list in forward order; zone ID order and within-zone head insertion age are distinct determinants of processing order.
findings.limitations: Full zone-map creation and relocation sequence for a particular editable workspace was not replayed.

findings.claim: A non-sentinel height stamped by an earlier object can seed a later overlapping object's entire footprint and propagate through a chain of overlapping regions without endpoint objects touching; the final result depends on scan priority and other preexisting heights.
findings.limitations: Seven analytical scenarios only; not live original-code execution and not tied to shipped authoring workspaces.

findings.claim: After grading, the editor clears EAX, zero-extends a 16-bit work-plane height into EAX, then compares it to 0xffffffff before assigning object+0x0C; the equality branch is unreachable for that zero-extended sample.
findings.limitations: No original editor runtime experiment measures the effect when the sampled value equals the 0x8000 sentinel.

findings.claim: Road-neighbor interpolator 00421BE0 only enters its existing-height material update branch when the material index is below 6; surface 6/7 protection is conditional on a non-sentinel work-plane height.
findings.limitations: This does not prove universal immunity from other terrain grading stages.

findings.claim: The four smoothing sweeps iterate active zones sequentially; 00422870 copies each zone's scratch output back before processing the next zone and reads neighbors from global height plane 1, so boundaries can observe already-updated earlier zones in the same sweep.
findings.limitations: Global non-simultaneity is an instruction-derived scheduling implication. The toy average does not reproduce exact x87 rounding or bit-identical output.

findings.claim: Existing v20 records show 381 of 386 polygon footprints contain surface 6 or 7, but most of the 19 largest documented worst-point height gaps occur at material 0 or 1; editor overlap mechanism alone does not explain these retail anomalies.
findings.limitations: The editor workspace source is missing; no direct authored-object footprint to retail-terrain match or causal claim.
